Show HN: Export your Character.AI chats in minutes – open-source, runs locally
items.summary: Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 in October, and the auction of the company is scheduled for November 23. Its built-in data export can take three to four weeks, and the download link expires after seven days. People with years of conversations have been asking how to keep a copy before anything changes. This is a small browser extension for Chrome and Firefox (Manifest V3). On a character.ai tab you press its button, and it reads your own chats, characters, personas and memory boxes from the site's web API with the session you are already signed in with, one request at a time, and saves one JSON file, plus plain text if you want it. Every line keeps who wrote it and when, which the official export does not. It asks for no permissions in advance (activeTab and scripting), only reads, talks to nothing but character.ai, and has no analytics or servers. The code in src/ is what runs: nothing is bundled or minified. MIT license. Disclosure: we make Amavie, an AI character app. We also built a free viewer that opens the file, or the official export ZIP, in the browser without uploading it: https://amavie.ai/character-ai-export . The extension does not need an account with us. The store listings are in review; until then, unzip the Chrome build from Releases and load it unpacked. Feedback is welcome, especially from very large accounts.

items.title: Show HN: Kairos – Open-source risk and fraud decisioning platform
items.summary: Hey HN, Ayan here from Finic. We’re launching Kairos, an open source alternative to Sift, Sardine, and other real-time fraud decisioning platforms. Kairos addresses two of the biggest problems facing traditional decisioning tools: a lack of labeled data to train on and dealing with fraudsters that are constantly changing their tactics. 1. Traditional fraud solutions use ML models such as XGBoost to detect fraud, but these models are dependent on quality labeled data which many businesses do not have. We address this by using “System One” decision models in additional to traditional models such as XGBoost and logistic regression. This allows you to incorporate plain language questions such as “Is this a throwaway email” into your decisioning, bypassing the need for large amounts of labeled data. This also allows you to capture aspects of fraud that are more unstructured, which is something that XGBoost models struggle with. 2. Fraud teams are facing off with live players that are constantly changing their behavior to bypass the detection logic they have in place. You can train a detection model or define a ruleset once, but it will become obsolete in a matter of weeks as fraudsters figure out what your detection logic is. This means that you need a team regularly training models and updating rules based on new fraud patterns. Typically this takes a large data science/ML team. Kairos addresses this by introducing an MCP server, so that your agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.) can define a decision workflow, train models on your data, and pick the variant that performs best. You can self-host Kairos with Docker or use the hosted version at https://kairos.finic.ai

items.title: Show HN: I got tired of GitHub trending, so I built my own
items.summary: I like to see what new projects people are working on in open-source, but I found it hard to find projects or news in any systematic way. I built Shadowgraph so that I could browse the latest in open source development in a more natural way. It ingests repos from github and scrapes hackernews, reddit, and X for mentions of them. I also identify noteworthy contributors on github and track what they're starring as a signal for potentially high quality projects that might otherwise fly under the radar. I also track their tweets or hackernews contributions for mentions of github repos for a more curated feed of content. Finally, there's an MCP and semantic search for repos and developers. This is a fun side project for me but I want it to be useful for people- feedback is very much appreciated.
